newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Cenbank sees T-bill in 6 wks-Casas.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Cenbank sees T-bill in 6 wks-Casas.

text.p: Venezuela's Central Bank expects to begin issuing treasury bills within the next six weeks, Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez said.

But the long awaited bills, to be issued by the Central Bank on behalf of the government, "will not completely substitute for the Central Bank TEMs currently used in open market operations," Casas said at a congressional committee.
"We expect to begin issuing them (the T-bills) within the next six weeks," he added.

The T-bills will be used to meet interest payments on some $4 billion of Treasury debt with the Central Bank that stems from the 1990s when the Bank stumped-up collateral for Venezuela's Brady debt restructuring.

Casas did not provide details on the characteristics of the bills. But according to legislation approved by Congress in the first week of February, bills worth at least 0.75 percent of Gross Domestic Product (some $480 million) will be issued each year.
The first year of payments will also see the Central Bank place an additional amount equivalent to 150 billion bolivars ($319 million), the legislation said.
